details: The US government's borrowing costs have reached levels not seen since 2007, with 30-year Treasury yields surpassing 5.18%. This surge is attributed to the ongoing Iran conflict, high US producer prices, and increasing federal debt. The situation is impacting all asset classes, including Bitcoin, which saw over $1 billion in ETF outflows in May as investors shifted towards safer assets like tokenized US Treasuries.
sourceName: Editorial Team (referencing macro analysis and market data)
title: US Borrowing Costs Hit Pre-Crisis Highs, Affecting Crypto Markets

details: Optimism for a diplomatic breakthrough in the US-Iran conflict is growing, with President Trump signaling a potential agreement soon. This positive sentiment has led to a decrease in oil prices and a rally in traditional financial markets, as geopolitical risk premiums ease. While cryptocurrencies showed a slower initial response, analysts suggest a finalized deal could pave the way for a recovery in the crypto market as global uncertainty diminishes.
title: US-Iran Peace Deal Hopes Drive Global Market Rally

details: China's new bank lending in May increased less than anticipated, showing only a modest recovery from the previous month's contraction. This is primarily due to a prolonged downturn in the property sector, which continues to curb household borrowing and overall demand. The situation highlights an uneven economic recovery and an increasing reliance on fiscal policy for stability. China maintains its strict ban on cryptocurrency trading.
title: China's May Loans Miss Forecasts Amid Property Slump

details: The European Central Bank has implemented its first interest rate hike since 2023, citing a broadening of inflation across the Eurozone, further aggravated by the Iran war's effect on energy prices. Concurrently, US inflation accelerated to 4.2% in May, reaching its fastest pace in over three years. These policy tightening measures indicate tighter global liquidity and increased market volatility.
title: ECB Raises Rates Amid Accelerating US Inflation and Iran War Impact

details: Polish President Andrzej Duda has vetoed a cryptocurrency regulation bill for the second time, returning it to parliament for reconsideration. This repeated action prolongs regulatory uncertainty for crypto businesses and investors in Poland, potentially delaying the establishment of a clear legal framework and alignment with the European Union's Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation.
title: Polish President Vetoes Crypto Regulation Bill Again
